notable_absence.finding: collect-logs.md never explains WHAT is redacted (which fields, whether user data or only identifying metadata) - only that a redacted copy exists and where it is written ('The redacted zip directory will be prefixed by `redacted-`'). A reader deciding whether it is safe to send unredacted logs to Support has no on-page way to know what the redaction actually removes.

cross_component_finding: This is the second page in the corpus (after a round-18 note's passing mention on eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.md) to reference cbcollect_info, and the first to give it a load-bearing role rather than a passing one: collect-logs' own --salt flag is deliberately designed to match cbcollect_info's salt so the two tools' redacted logs can be cross-referenced. That is real evidence the two log-collection tools are meant to be used together during a single support investigation, even though neither is documented as depending on the other.
cross_product_finding: The --upload-host/--customer/--ticket flow for uploading collected logs directly to Couchbase Support ('uploads.couchbase.com') is Server-tooling-specific; no equivalent surfaced in this batch's reading and the module framing (no Capella twin for cbbackupmgr) holds here without qualification.
